text:
Response B is better. It stays under the 120-word limit, at roughly 110 words, and keeps the points a manager needs: the price rises and data boosts with dates, which plans are affected, the no-exit-fee switching window, the remaining repayments caveat, and the reason. Its one weakness is grouping Classic plan customers with fixed-contract customers under "unaffected until their contract ends," which slightly blurs the Classic case, since those customers are simply unaffected this year. Response A is more precise on that point and clearer in layout, but at roughly 200 words it breaks the explicit length limit. It also includes support-channel details a busy manager doesn't need. Those extra words don't add enough to justify the overrun.

Verdict: B
